item.title: FSU head coach hot board 2.0
item.description: The FSU Seminoles have hired Jeff Purinton as their athletic director, and they have shifted their focus to finding their next head coach. He was the final piece they needed and is set to lead the search, alongside University President Richard McCullough, Board of Trustees Chair Peter Collins, and Daniel Parker of Parker Executive Search. The work can get started in earnest, although Purinton admitted on Tuesday that most of the work will not be public, as coaches are never willing to have conversations with another school during the season. Some of that has already taken place, with one candidate signing an extension and removing his name from the race. The Seminoles will not have a ton of time to make the hire, with the early signing period set to start on Dec. 2, giving them just a few days to get someone in after they end the season against the Florida Gators on Nov. 27 and most teams ending the regular season on Nov. 28. The transfer portal, which will be key for FSU to rebuild its roster, will open on Jan.4. Here is an updated look at the top names to watch as FSU football's head coaching search continues, as well as candidates who have seemingly lost some steam. Manny Diaz, Duke head coach Diaz could be one of the biggest winners of the Purinton hire. The two started their career at FSU in the '90s, and he has been heavily linked to the opening, going so far as to address it with his Duke team. He failed at Miami, but has excelled in his second stint as a head coach with several shrewd moves in the transfer portal. At 7-2, they are still alive in the ACC race, but have to beat Miami this week. Glenn Schumann, Georgia defensive coordinator If FSU does not hire a head coach, Schumann has emerged as the top coordinator to consider. Just like Diaz, he has worked with Purinton, with them both climbing the ranks at Alabama from 2008-15 until he followed Kirby Smart to Georgia. He has seen firsthand how the two best programs in modern college football have operated in Alabama and Georgia and looks ready to lead a program. Jimbo Fisher, former FSU head coach Fisher has made it abundantly clear that he wants to return to FSU, but it is unclear how enthusiastic FSU is about bringing him back. While he led FSU to the 2013 National Championship and a playoff berth in 2014, he has struggled ever since. He ultimately departed FSU in 2017 for Texas A&M, where he was fired in 2023 after going 45-25. Kenny Dillingham, Arizona State head coach Dillingham spent time at FSU under Mike Norvell and led Arizona State to the CFP in 2024. He has already turned down bigger jobs to stay with the Sun Devils, his alma mater, but it is worth seeing if the Seminoles can poach him, even if it is unlikely. item.title: Kentucky vs. Florida viewing info, what to watch for, odds, and predictions
item.description: Kentucky Football is now in the home stretch of the regular season, and their latest test will come against Jon Sumrall and the Florida Gators on Saturday. Kickoff is set for 6:15 PM ET on ESPN. Kentucky is coming off a humbling defeat last week on the road at Tennessee. The trip to Knoxville gave the Wildcats their second loss of the year and a drop in the College Football Playoff rankings. Will Stein’s Wildcats are now ranked No. 11 in the College Football Playoff rankings, which makes one point clear: Win, and you’re in. Kentucky has only three games left this season, and if they win them, they will find themselves in the bracket, playing for a National Championship in year one of the Will Stein era. It’s great to think about the postseason and how Big Blue Nation would feel about Stein making such a splash in year one, but business comes first. Stein always talks about one play at a time. In this instance, one game at a time. The next game is against a Florida team with a lot of ties. Over the last few years, as he made his way up the coaching ranks, Kentucky fans were begging to have Jon Sumrall be the successor when Mark Stoops calls it a career in Lexington. Sumrall played at Kentucky and spent years on the sidelines in various coaching roles, primarily as an inside linebacker coach. Well, Sumrall made his climb quickly, and the timeline lined up to where it could potentially happen, but it didn’t. Florida would have a head-coaching vacancy to fill, and, other than Lane Kiffin, Sumrall was the one guy they had in mind for the job. Sumrall took the job, and after Stoops was let go of his duties, his defensive coordinator, Brad White, took the same role under Sumrall in Gainesville. As for connections on the other side, Kentucky defensive backs Aaron Gates and Jordan Castell both played at Florida before transferring to play at Kentucky under new defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, who also spent a couple of seasons under the last regime at Florida. Now, all those connections in this game create a ton of motivation on both sides to win, as if an SEC game wasn’t enough already. After the brutal, ready-to-forget night in Knoxville last weekend, Kentucky enters this contest as a field-goal favorite over the Gators. After years and years of losing to Florida, Stoops flipped the script toward the end of his time at the helm at Kentucky, winning four of the last five against them before he was let go. Florida has been struggling in the last few weeks, but has shown the ability to dominate teams at times, so Kentucky will have to be locked in with the old SEC East rival coming to town. item.title: IMG Academy vs. St. Frances in monster football game: Here's who to watch
item.description: The grudge match of the 2026 season has finally arrived. IMG Academy and St. Frances Academy (Md.) have lost no love for each other, and have had the regular season finale circled on their calendars since spring workouts. The two national powerhouses were slated to play in what would have been considered a national championship last year, but IMG Academy canceled the game a few days before it was set to be played . The Ascenders were accused of an unforgivable crime in the high school football world — ducking smoke. "But I think this shows you that, money, resources can’t necessarily buy team chemistry and it creates for an environment that’s not worth sending your child to," St. Frances head coach Messay Hailemariam told Rivals . "I’ll be honest with you, because for them to make a decision based on their success as an institution as opposed to the success of the young people that are willing to compete, for me, it makes me think twice about having to put our kids in these type of situations again.” IMG Academy made sure a game against the Panthers was one of the first to be set in the schedule this year, and they have been using every game as a building block towards a final heavyweight bout. "We're coming hungry (this year)," IMG quarterback Jayden Wade told USA TODAY in February. "We've got a lot still to prove. On the internet, everyone is saying we ducked St. Frances — but that's not the truth. I think we've still got something to prove, we're on a mission." The Ascenders will travel to Maryland to take on St. Frances at Bowie State on Nov. 13. Here are three Ascenders to watch in the high-stakes matchup: Jayden Wade, 2027 QB Wade's had this game circled on his calendar for a long time, and the five-star Georgia commit loves to make a statement. The junior signal caller has been surgical for IMG this year, tossing for just under 2,000 yards and 23 touchdowns on a 72% completion rate and just two picks. Elijah Newman-Hall, 2028 RB The Ohio State commit was incredible against the Hun School , rushing for three touchdowns and 116 yards on 16 touches. Newman-Hall is a powerful, balanced ball carrier that is taking full advantage of an offensive line finding its form. He'll be invaluable again against St. Frances, which fell to Hun 14-9 last month. Jackson Vaughn, 2027 EDGE Vaughn has been stuffing the stat sheet for the Ascenders, and they'll look to him more than ever before this year against St. Frances. The Notre Dame commit is up to 20 tackles for loss and seven sacks, but just as important is how he disrupts passing lanes. He's tallied two interceptions and three pass breakups at the line of scrimmage this year. item.title: What do you need to see out of Germany when it squares off vs. Serbia?
item.description: (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jürgen Klopp and Germany have another opportunity to build momentum when they take on Serbia, but this fixture should be about more than simply getting a result. Klopp is still in the discovery phase of his tenure, evaluating his options, experimenting with different combinations, and figuring out which players can become part of his long-term plans. With the 2026 World Cup approaching, there is still plenty of work to do. That makes this another important opportunity for Germany to show signs of progress. First and foremost, the team needs to demonstrate a clearer identity. Klopp’s preferred style should gradually become more recognizable, particularly when it comes to pressing, intensity, winning the ball back quickly, and transitioning into attack. Germany have enough individual quality to hurt almost any opponent, but that talent needs to translate into a cohesive collective performance. There are also individual performances worth watching. Which players are making a convincing case for more responsibility? Can the established names provide the leadership and consistency Klopp needs? Are some of the younger prospects ready to make the jump and become genuine options for the senior team? The result obviously matters, but it should not necessarily be the defining measurement of this particular stage of Klopp’s project. Germany need to start looking like a team with a clear direction rather than a collection of talented individuals still figuring things out. A convincing performance, improved defensive organization, greater attacking fluidity, and some encouraging individual displays would all represent positive steps. So, what is your biggest priority for Germany against Serbia? Do you want to see a dominant performance and a convincing victory, or are you more interested in seeing Klopp make tactical progress, identify his best players, and give the next generation an opportunity to impress? item.title: Interceptions have dried up for No. 10 Cougars’ defense. Why the drought?
item.description: BYU Cougars defensive back Evan Johnson (0) intercepts the ball during a game against Utah Tech at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo on Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News In 2024, BYU led the country in interceptions per game, snagging 22 picks in 13 games. Last year, the Cougars had 17 interceptions in 14 games, tying for 11th in the country in total interceptions. BYU’s defense started the highly anticipated 2026 season in similar fashion, getting six interceptions in their first four games. Since then, however, the well has dried up. The No. 10 Cougars (7-2, 4-2) have gone their last five games — compiling a 3-2 record in that stretch — without having picked off an opposing quarterback. What’s going on? “It’s just one of those things,” BYU defensive coordinator Kelly Poppinga said Wednesday, with a grimace, as the Cougars continued preparations to host Baylor (6-3, 4-2) on Saturday at LaVell Edwards Stadium. The Cougars have dropped to 71st in the country in total interceptions. The irony is that BYU is tied for third in the nation in pass breakups, with 47. Utah and Clemson are tied for the most, with 48. No team in the nation over the course of the last five games has more PBUs than BYU, which has 34 during that stretch. “We work our turnover circuit every single week, and yeah, we’re getting our hands on the ball better than anybody in the country right now, especially in the last five games,” Poppinga said. “We got to finish them and honestly get the right (breaks). We got to get lucky bounces too as well. … The ball has just got to bounce your way, especially those tipped balls at the line of scrimmage.” Opponents have nine interceptions against BYU, and 27 PBUs. Of course, BYU’s secondary has not been at full strength since the opener when starting safety Raider Damuni went down for a bunch of games. Then all-conference corner Evan “Schmev” Johnson was injured in the 39-31 loss at UCF. He hasn’t returned, and is listed as doubtful for Baylor. “When the opportunities come, we have to be there. item.title: ‘Elite pocket passer’ Jared Goff not being underestimated by Patriots
item.description: No matter where you go on Al Gore’s internet, whenever there is a list of the NFL’s best quarterbacks you find familiar faces near the top. Mahomes, Allen, Burrow, sometimes — when he has his turnover tendencies under control — Maye. Jared Goff, on the other hand, typically resides further down the list. It can’t be due to a lack of production, at least this year: Goff has been one of the most efficient quarterbacks in football while leading the Detroit Lions to a 6-2 record. But while fans and analysts might be underestimating the 32-year-old, his next opponent sure is not. The New England Patriots are well aware of the damage he has done, and is capable of doing this Sunday in Munich. “I think Jared’s playing at a high level,” said head coach Mike Vrabel. “Continued the last three years, he’s been at a high level.” “He’s an elite pocket passer,” linebacker Robert Spillane added. “He loves to step up in the middle of the pocket and deliver the ball downfield. Really can do it all. First overall pick for a reason, who just continued throughout his career to show why he was a first overall pick. Somebody who’s going to get the ball to all of his guys.” Distributing the ball to the weapons mentioned by Spillane, as well as to NFL scrimmage yards leader Jahmyr Gibbs, Goff has played some of the best football of his career so far in 2026. The numbers show it, too. In eight games thus far, he has completed over two thirds of his passes (185 of 273) for 2,134 yards, 15 touchdowns and just two interceptions. Whether you use traditional metrics or advanced ones such as EPA or CPOE Goff typically finds himself in the top 10 if not close to the league lead. He might not be the same big-play hunter as the quarterback the Patriots faced last week, Green Bay’s Jordan Love, but Goff has been steady and operating well within Detroit’s offensive system. “The quarterback runs the show very well,” said defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr. “He gets them into plays for the whole unit, and he kind of has the freedom to do that.” There might not be one particular part about Goff’s game or his physical abilities that stands out relative to other quarterbacks, which might contribute to his perception. However, that does not mean he cannot put intense pressure on any defense. A large part of that is his willingness to disperse the football, and the chemistry and experience he has built with the players surrounding him. “He’s a great quarterback,” said safety Kevin Byard. “He does a great job when he’s able to stand in the middle of the pocket, he can fire across the middle of the field, deep, with obviously the weapons that they have with Jameson Williams, a guy who can stretch the field, and obviously Amon-Ra St. Brown, who’s a guy who can work the middle of the field, work the intermediates and things like that. item.description: The Michigan football team is 5-4 in coach Kyle Whittingham's first season. The Wolverines have lost two of their past three games and face three ranked teams in their final three games. Whittingham coached the previous 21 seasons at Utah. (Photo by Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images) Getty Images When Michigan hired Kyle Whittingham as its football coach last December, the Wolverines hoped he could bring some stability to a program that had endured multiple controversies in recent seasons. At 66 years old, Whittingham was a veteran presence and a consistent winner in 21 seasons at Utah. But in his first season at Michigan, Whittingham has struggled, while his former program has shined. Michigan is 5-4 and unranked in the Associated Press and College Football Playoff polls. The Wolverines are going to be underdogs in their final three regular season games, too, as they travel to No. 16 on Oregon on Saturday, face No. 4 UCLA at home on Nov. 21 and visit No. 20 Ohio State on Nov. 28. Utah, meanwhile, is 9-0 and No. 2 in the AP poll and CFP rankings. The Utes are one of only two undefeated teams in the nation, along with UCLA, and are thriving under Morgan Scalley, who was Whittingham’s defensive coordinator since 2016 before getting promoted to head coach when Whittingham resigned. At the time, Whittingham did not have a job lined up. In fact, earlier that month, he told University officials he wanted to remain at Utah, according to Yahoo Sports, which obtained documents via a public records request. But when the sides couldn’t agree on a new contract, Whittingham departed. Two weeks later, he was introduced as Michigan’s coach, replacing Sherrone Moore, who was fired for cause for allegedly engaging in an inappropriate relationship with a staffer. item.description: Motorsport photo Iker Lecuona had to adapt to a different Ducati during the MotoGP weekend in Qatar. Having previously ridden Fermin Aldeguer's GP25, the Spaniard took over Alex Marquez's bike in Losail, giving him access to the latest specification of the Desmosedici. Asked about the differences between the two Ducati versions, Lecuona said: "It feels different, feels different. We need to ride in a little bit different style, let's say. You know, you can see the difference on the aerodynamics, and I can feel the difference." The World Superbike rider has made several recent appearances for Gresini Ducati this year. After impressing with his performance in Hungary, he replaced the injured Aldeguer in Australia and Malaysia before stepping in for Marquez in Losail. This meant switching from the GP25 to the GP26 within a relatively short period. Adapting to the latest Ducati "was not easy" The change came at an inconvenient time for the 26-year-old. After several weeks on the same bike, he had to get used to a different overall package immediately before the Qatar weekend. "After two weeks, almost three weeks with the same bike, then coming with that one, it was not easy to adapt and to learn," he said. Despite the additional work involved, his overall assessment was positive. The Spaniard viewed the weekend as an important learning opportunity and gave himself a high mark for his performance. "But, I did almost like nine in my notes for this exam. This weekend I put a nine because I think I learned a lot, I improved a lot," he said. Iker Lecuona, Gresini Racing Iker Lecuona, Gresini Racing Lecuona finished ninth in the sprint and 10th in the grand prix, scoring points in both races. MotoGP experience an advantage for WorldSBK The 26-year-old normally rides for Ducati's factory team in WSBK. He also sees his MotoGP outings as an opportunity to gain valuable experience for his future in the series. Asked what specific lessons he could take back to WorldSBK, Lecuona highlighted several areas: "The way to brake with the Michelin, the way to manage the tyre, the way to work with the body [of the bike], to understand what I miss on the bike. So that is the main difference and help me for the future." Those lessons could prove particularly useful in the long term, given that WorldSBK will switch from Pirelli to Michelin tyres next season. item.title: ‘It’s a lie’ – Rogers defends Palmer over England commitment
item.description: ‘It’s a lie’ – Rogers defends Palmer over England commitment Morgan Rogers has strongly defended Cole Palmer and insisted it is “a lie” to suggest the Chelsea attacker does not want to play for England. Palmer was left out of Thomas Tuchel’s latest squad having missed previous squads through injury, with the England boss admitting he has “missed too many opportunities to impress”. But Rogers, who has known Palmer since they were teenagers together at Manchester City and is now his team-mate at Chelsea, says there should be no doubt over his commitment to the national team. “It’s a lie. He wants to be here,” Rogers told BBC Radio 5 Live. “He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing. “We all know he had a difficult year last year with injuries and I know personally he’s been managing them injuries ever since. “He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn’t feel 100 per cent himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself.” Rogers added that Palmer has to manage his body with the bigger picture in mind. “If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it,” he said. “It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It’s a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England.” Asked if he wants to see Palmer back in the England side, Rogers replied: “Of course I do. What a player he is. “He’s got so much quality, so much ability. Hopefully sooner rather than later.” Tuchel was later asked about Rogers’ comments and said: “It is totally fine. It is his teammate and I guess his friend, so why wouldn’t he make an emotional statement? “All I can say is, I am very happy with the emotional commitment from Morgan and the physical commitment of Morgan Rogers.”

item.title: “Made No Sense”: NFL Insider Questions Giants’ Baffling Play-Calling After Heartbreaking Loss to Commanders
item.description: John Harbaugh - OTA Press Conference © Imagn The New York Giants had a chance to strengthen their grip on the NFC East, but a late-game collapse against the Washington Commanders turned Thursday night’s loss into a missed opportunity. Despite holding a 21-17 lead with less than a minute remaining, the Giants gave up a late touchdown and eventually fell 24-21. NFL insider Ari Meirov questioned New York’s decision-making during its final offensive possession. The team tried to make deep passes despite having two timeouts available. “Throwing deep shots with two timeouts made no sense,” Meirov wrote on X, criticizing the Giants’ approach. New York was doing really well earlier, and it even looked like they would win after J.J. McCarthy connected with Isaiah Likely for a 66-yard touchdown, giving the Giants a four-point advantage. However, Jayden Daniels responded with Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with just 57 seconds remaining. The Commanders reclaimed the lead, leaving McCarthy and the Giants with one final opportunity. Later, McCarthy’s final deep attempt toward Malik Nabers was intercepted by Rasul Douglas, sealing Washington’s victory. With two timeouts still available, New York had opportunities to use shorter passes and potentially work its way into scoring position. Instead, the decision to attempt deep shots left little room for error. The questionable approach was frustrating, given how well the Giants’ offense had performed early. McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards and a touchdown. Cam Skattebo also contributed two rushing touchdowns . John Harbaugh Reacts After Giants Surrender Late Lead After the defeat, Harbaugh acknowledged that his team played well in several areas but ultimately failed to do enough to secure the win. “We played a pretty good football game too, just not good enough to win the game. We have a good spirit; it’s not one of fear. It’s one of power and courage. We’ll continue fighting,” Harbaugh said. The Giants’ head coach also said that the loss would not change the team’s broader objectives. “It’s a missed opportunity, but like I told the guys – it would’ve been great to win the game, but it doesn’t change our goals or our opportunity going forward. It’s a tough loss. It’s the National Football League; you’re going to lose some games,” added Harbaugh. New York now sits at 5-3-1, with the Commanders improving to 3-5-1 following their divisional victory. The Giants will have little time to dwell on the disappointment, as the Jacksonville Jaguars are waiting for them in Week 11.
